newsitem.title: USA: Marathon, Ashland form oil refining venture.
newsitem.headline: Marathon, Ashland form oil refining venture.

text.p: USX Corp. and Ashland Inc. said Thursday they would combine their oil refining, marketing and transportation operations in a bid to cut costs in the competitive and profit-squeezed industry.
The move was the latest venture by major oil companies to try to bolster results in refining and marketing, including one announced in March between Shell Oil Co. and Texaco Inc.

Under the deal, USX's USX-Marathon Group subsidiary will own a 62 percent stake in the venture, which will include Ashland's refinery-produced petrochemicals. Ashland, based in Ashland, Ky., will own 38 percent.

The companies said they expect the joint venture to achieve substantial benefits by becoming more efficient and integrating operations. There are no plans to close major plants but future decisions will depend on business conditions, they added.

"The goal of this joint venture is to create a competitive enterprise which capitalises on the strengths and complementary assets of both companies," said Thomas Usher, chairman of Pittsburgh-based USX. "Market conditions have dictated that new approaches be explored to improve performance and growth opportunities."

Ashland Chief Executive Officer Paul Chellgren said the companies expect to finalise the deal by the end of the year. The transaction is subject to approval by regulators and the boards of USX and Ashland.
Chellgren said he did not expect any big regulatory hurdles.
"We don't expect any difficulties because the business continues to be extraordinarily competitive," he said in a telephone interview.

The companies said job cuts and reassignments were likely, but did not specify how many workers would be affected. Chellgren declined to discuss potential cost savings or job cuts, saying more review was needed.
He said the two companies had been in talks about the alliance since last year.

The venture, to be based in Findlay, Ohio, will not include the companies' exploration, production and chemical businesses. Other exclusions include Ashland's Valvoline division, along with equity investments in certain pipelines for both companies.

Current plans are to maintain the existing brands of each company. Marathon Oil Co., part of USX-Marathon, markets its products under the Marathon as well as other brands through its Emro Marketing Co. -- Speedway, Bonded, Cheker, Starvin' Marvin, United, Gastown, Wake Up and Kwik Sak. Ashland brands include Ashland, Super America and Rich Oil.

J. L. "Corky" Frank, Marathon's executive vice president of refining, marketing and transportation, will become president of the venture, which has yet to be named. Duane Gilliam, Ashland Petroleum's executive vice president, will become executive vice president.

For Ashland, the joint venture represents the latest move in a reorganization under the leadership of company veteran Chellgren, who recently assumed the top posts upon the retirement of longtime head John Hall.
Ashland announced several moves in December to restructure its core business and enhance profitability.

Separately, Chellgren confirmed that Ashland is in talks to sell its exploration unit instead of spinning it off to shareholders as had been planned. Sources familiar with the transaction said the unit, Blazer Energy Corp., is expected to be sold for about $600 million.
"We have taken bids. We are evaluating those bids. We are currently in negotiations with the people who appear most likely," Chellgren said.
Sources identified the leading candidates as Equitable Resources Inc. and privately held Eastern Group, which is 83-percent owned by Norway's Statoil. Both potential buyers declined to comment.
Ashland's stock rose $1 to $46.50, while Marathon rose 62.5 cents to $28.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
